title: Adaptive micro-tranches with focus signals and staff rotation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: During cycles we observe large variances in throughput across initiatives, leading to bursty pull requests, last-minute scope cuts, and uneven engineer utilization. Goal: Design an operational pattern that slices cycle commits into predictable micro-tranches (~2-week micro-scope windows) and exposes clear focus signals so teams can rotate staff, accept temporary trade-offs, and make fast scope cuts without undermining core OKRs. Success metrics: 1) reduce mid-cycle scope rework by 40% versus baseline, 2) raise mean team utilization smoothing index by 25%, 3) <10% of features delayed due to staffing contention. This ticket captures the product play and rollout plan for micro-tranches, focus signals, surge lanes, and staff rotation rules.
proposal_summary: Introduce 'micro-tranches' as first-class cycle units: each micro-tranche is a small, independently shippable subset of an initiative (~1-2 engineer-weeks). Add explicit 'Focus Signals' per micro-tranche (Go/Slow/Cut) derived from OKR confidence, customer impact, and technical risk. Implement an Ops rubric and a lightweight dashboard for capacity signals. Pair this with a staff rotation protocol that designates a 20% 'flow rotation pool' per squad to accept transient context switching during micro-tranche transitions.
tradeoffs: Pros: smoother capacity usage, earlier risk discovery, cleaner scope cuts. Cons: increased coordination overhead, possible fragmentation of work context, requires discipline in defining minimal micro-tranches. Risk of gaming Focus Signals if incentives not aligned. Engineering must accept some context switch costs; design/PM must tighten acceptance criteria for micro-tranche scope.
rollout_plan: 1) Pilot with two cross-functional squads in Cycle 2025-W04 (one infra-heavy, one product-heavy). 2) Build simple dashboard (OKR confidence + queued work + staffing signals) for PMs and Eng leads in first week. 3) Run 2 micro-tranches in pilot teams, collect qualitative feedback. 4) Iterate rubric and expand to four squads next cycle. 5) Bake into cycle planning templates and templates in Confluence and the Cycle Ops playbook.
operational_rubric: Micro-tranche sizing: 20-40 story points or <=2 engineer-weeks. Focus Signals: GO (high confidence, ship), SLOW (requires more validation), CUT (deprioritize if capacity constrained). Cut criteria: low user impact, high implementation risk, non-critical dependency. Surge lane policy: each org may request up to one short-term surge (max 3 FTE-weeks) with approval from Product Lead + Eng Lead. Staff rotation: rotation pool should include at least one engineer with domain context per team to minimize rework.
metrics_and_dashboards: Dashboard KPIs: micro-tranche completion rate, fraction of tranche scope cut mid-cycle, mean time-to-decision for Focus Signals, engineer context switch index. Data sources: JIRA/Linear tags, Cycle Console capacity panel, velocity snapshots. Initial dashboard prototype: https://dash.redwood.internal/cycle-microtranches (internal).
